note: Pre-registered holdout splits (KAN-38). A split may carry `min_sessions`: the shortest window it may be spent on, enforced by scripts/run_sleeve_evaluation.py BEFORE the burn, so a window too short to carry a claim costs nothing. Absent means no minimum was registered -- a fact about that split's provenance, not a licence. A split is written down here BEFORE it is looked at, and research/evaluation/holdout.py records its single evaluation in the `evaluations` list below. Commit the burn when it happens: a holdout whose use is not in git is a holdout on the honour system. `registered_at` is caller-supplied and therefore backdatable -- the evidence of record is this file's git commit date, not the field. Key order matches holdout.py's writer so recording a burn produces a minimal diff.

Forward split registered 2026-09-14, BEFORE any evaluation looked at a single session inside it, and boundary-dated after the 2026-08-28 burn of incumbent_sleeves_2026. Registered now because today is the last day this window is unlooked-at: registration is free, and a boundary written down after someone has seen the bars it covers is not a pre-registration. SCOPE. Valid for any candidate whose search predates 2026-08-29. The two known cases are the sentiment thread's gate evaluation (merged 2026-08-04, clock set for 2026-11) and the native factor catalog (specified 2026-08-02, four factors, trial_registry.json). It is SINGLE-USE, so spending it on one forecloses the other -- decide which before running, and register a second split for the other rather than arguing this one covers both after the fact. NOT valid for the six incumbent sleeves. They were judged on 2026-08-28 (all six FAIL) and their re-judgement under the corrected benchmark-relative null spends NO holdout: the corrected null can only strengthen a FAIL, and a split spent re-confirming a negative is a split gone. See docs/operations/incumbent-edge-evaluation.md. TWO LIMITS, both binding. (1) Out-of-SEARCH-sample, not out-of-sight-sample. The paper book trades this window daily and is watched daily, so no live-overlapping window can ever be out-of-sight; out-of-search is the honest ceiling and this split reaches it. (2) NO ADMISSIBLE BASELINE REACHES PAST THE BOUNDARY YET. The pinned, bias-accepted artifact backtest_multi_20260819_183451.json ends 2026-08-18, so resolve() raises against it rather than returning an empty window. The only artifact that reaches further, backtest_multi_20260910_235624.json, carries coverage 17.39% excluded against a 5.00% floor -- worse than the 11.28% D18 accepted, and bias_acceptances.json pins an acceptance to one sha256 and never widens. Spending this split therefore needs either a clean baseline or a new, deliberate bias acceptance larger than D18's. min_sessions 60 is the driver's own significance bar, now enforced before the burn instead of printed after it. 60 sessions from the boundary lands around late November 2026; the split cannot be spent before then and the attempt costs nothing.
